    Geographic focus:
        Asia, India, Delhi (Sunder Nagri slum, north-east Delhi)
    Temporal focus:
        T1. Historical observation [YES] — multi-year heatwave trend documented
        T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — policy submissions, planned legal action, new disaster classification
        T3. Long-term development [YES] — urban resilience policy, human rights framing, climate litigation
    Synopsis:
        Residents of a Delhi slum are documenting extreme heat experiences in community "heat diaries," recording ground-surface temperatures exceeding 54°C. The project, led by Greenpeace India, aims to fill critical data gaps in India's heat action planning by capturing lived, granular human experiences. Testimonies have been submitted to India's National Human Rights Commission and are being developed into legal evidence. India's August 2024 decision to classify heatwaves as national disasters adds policy momentum. The article highlights the acute socioeconomic burden of extreme heat on low-income urban communities.
